composition.story: Eight trials start with one epoch each. After every round, successive halving ranks trials by their current score, drops the lower half, and doubles the epochs for survivors. Each round costs the same eight epochs, so training concentrates on trials that keep ranking well.

aha.observation: Rank, cut the lower half, double the survivors' epochs: every round costs 8 epochs, so trial C reached 4 epochs for 24 total instead of 32.

variants.label: Eight trials, keep top half each round (accuracy %, higher is better)

states.label: Start
states.sentence: Eight untrained trials share one budget. Nothing is scored yet, so none can be preferred.
states.why: Halving needs scores before it can choose.

states.label: Round 1 training
states.sentence: Every trial trains one epoch and gets a score. G leads at 71; D trails at 48.
states.why: A cheap, equal budget gives a fair first ranking.

states.label: Cut to four
states.sentence: The top four scores survive: G 71, C 68, E 66, A 62. F, B, H and D stop.
states.why: The lower half is dropped; no more epochs go to it.

states.label: Round 2 training
states.sentence: The four survivors train to two epochs. C rises to 76 and passes G at 74.
states.why: Doubled budget per trial; the ranking can change.

states.label: Cut to two
states.sentence: Only C 76 and G 74 stay. E at 69 and A at 67 stop.
states.why: The same halving rule is applied to the survivors.

states.label: Round 3 training
states.sentence: C and G train to four epochs. C scores 81 and G scores 79.
states.why: Fewer trials now receive the largest budget.

states.label: Winner and cost
states.sentence: C wins at 81. Each round cost 8 epochs, so halving spent 24 versus 32 for training all eight to 4 epochs.
states.why: Survivors halve while epochs per trial double, holding round cost constant.
